Faculty Senate Executive Committee Bill #2026-2027-01 October 15, 2026 Faculty Senate Meeting - FOR ACTION (Introduced at the September 17, 2026 Faculty Senate Meeting) Creates standard process for committee formation Approved by FSEC 08/31/26 and 10/7/26 (as amended) Reviewed by CBUM 09/28/26 and 10/8/26 (as amended) Legislation effective date: Spring semester 2027 Rationale: The limited number of faculty senators, in combination with University-Manual-mandated committee staffing requirements, can make it difficult to staff an expanding number of standing committees.
This makes it important to ensure that additional standing committees and subcommittees, whose charges and memberships are proscribed in the University Manual, are created only in response to a significant and sustained need.
In contrast, special committees can be created by the Faculty Senate to address pressing issues.
While there is no limit to the length of time a special committee can exist, the faculty senate must vote to reauthorize each special committee each year.

This legislation mandates that a newly formed committee must exist as a special committee for at least three (3) years before legislation reconstituting it as a standing committee or subcommittee can be considered by the Faculty Senate.
Such legislation must be accompanied by language specifying the charge and membership of the standing committee for inclusion in the University Manual.
This change provides time for the Faculty Senate to 1) consider whether a new standing committee or subcommittee is truly warranted; and 2) craft an appropriate and achievable charge for the body.
This legislation does not mandate that a special committee must be reconstituted as a standing committee after three years.
It is also not retroactive, i.e., all existing standing committees and subcommittees remain unchanged.
This original version of this legislation was introduced for discussion at the 9/17/26 Faculty Senate meeting.
The final version has been revised as follows in response to faculty/staff comments. 1.
Remove language mentioning joint committees .
Joint committees are, by definition, created in concert with the administration (staffing, wording, charge, power balance).

While the faculty and administration may choose to designate a joint committee as a special joint committee subject to the rules and procedures detailed below, the power to do so does not rest exclusively with the faculty senate. 2.
Identify the assessment process and who conducts it.
Added language to §4.12.1 specifying that the Special Committee’s self-assessment shall be reviewed by FSEC.
FSEC which shall use it as the basis for a recommendation to the Faculty Senate to vote on whether the 1

Committee should dissolve, continue as a Special Committee, or be reconstituted as a permanent Standing Committee or Subcommittee. 3.
What happens if no reauthorization vote is taken before the end of the AY?
Added language to §4.11.1 specifying that all Special Committees are annually authorized by vote of the Faculty Senate.
A Special Committee that has not received an affirmative reauthorization vote (assuming that no duly authorized extension has been granted) within one year of authorization shall be dissolved. 4.
After the third-year review, can a reauthorized Special Committee apply to change its status?
Added language to §4.12.1 specifying that a Special Committee must wait at least two years after its third-year review (i.e., be in its fifth consecutive year of operation) before requesting that the Faculty Senate reconsider reconstituting it as a Standing Committee or Subcommittee.
